subject: RFI: Forensic exportability & retention matrix request
messages:
From: Megan Alvarez <megan.alvarez@megabank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.example>, procurement@megabank.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: RFI: forensic exportability & retention matrix request

Hi Hannah,

As part of MegaBank's vendor security assessment for our payments platform migration, we need a concise matrix showing Redwood's audit/log export capabilities and default retention behavior. Specifically we'd like answers to the following: 

- List of audit events captured (auth, token use, model selection, prompt transcripts, admin actions).
- Default retention windows per event type and whether configurable per-account.
- Procedures and SLAs for producing a forensic export (format, max time to delivery, expedited options).
- Supported export destinations (S3 presigned, streaming to SIEM, APIs) and sample output schema (JSON/CSV snippets).
- Legal hold / preservation features and whether retention can be suspended for a tenant.
- Encryption and key management for exported logs (customer-managed keys supported?).

We appreciate a single spreadsheet/matrix and a short playbook describing the export steps and security controls. Can you provide a draft and an example presigned S3 link (sanitized) so our infra team can validate ingestion?

Please CC procurement and Oliver Chen (security) on any follow-ups. We are targeting a security review by 4/5.

Thanks,
Megan Alvarez
IT Risk — MegaBank
megan.alvarez@megabank.com

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list.

We're pulling together a single-sheet retention/export matrix and a short export-playbook that covers S3 presigned exports, streaming options, formats, and legal-hold behavior. I'VE attached an initial draft matrix (redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a brief playbook stub (export_playbook_v1.pdf) for your team to review. 

Quick notes up front:
- We capture admin, auth, model selection, request/response transcripts (customer-controlled prompt retention), and system telemetry as separate event classes.
- Default retention is 90 days for transient request content (configurable to longer windows for Dedicated/Private deployments).
- Forensic exports can be produced via presigned S3 packages (preferred) or by streaming JSON to a customer SIEM; standard delivery SLA is typically 24 business hours, expedited 4 hours with a signed request and PoP.
- Customer-managed KMS supported in Private deployments; hosted customers can opt into a CMEK flow in Dedicated.

Can Karthik/Marissa help refine the matrix for the expedited/export SLAs and the sample artifact we're going to provide? We'll set a short call if you want a walkthrough.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Hannah / Marissa —

Looks good overall. A few suggestions before we send the updated package to Megan: 

1) Add explicit SLA rows: standard export turnaround = 24 hours (business), expedited = 4 hours (requires signed expedited request + confirmation of identity). Call out weekend handling.
2) Include an example presigned S3 URL as a sanitized sample file (s3_presigned_sample.txt) and demonstrate the package layout: metadata.json (manifest), events.ndjson (line-delimited JSON), checksums.sha256.
3) Clarify encryption: for hosted customers we rotate server-side keys; Dedicated customers can configure CMEK via AWS KMS; Private/on-prem supports HSM integration.
4) Under legal hold, state that for Hosted accounts we provide hold-on-export where we can extend retention for the tenant for an agreed period; for Dedicated/Private it's configurable and can be enforced by customer policy.

I'll update the matrix and playbook and flag the rows that require product/legal sign-off. Marissa — can you add the export manifest example and the sample NDJSON schema?

Karthik

Hi Megan / Oliver —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the updated retention & export package: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (updated), export_playbook_v1.pdf (expanded with manifest example), and s3_presigned_sample.txt (sanitized). Below is a short summary of the deliverables and how to validate ingestion into your S3/processing pipeline.

Summary highlights:
- Event classes captured: admin_event, auth_event, model_request, model_response, system_telemetry. Each class has a default retention window in the matrix; hosted defaults are 90 days for model_request/response and 365 days for admin_event; all are configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- Export formats: packaged tar.gz of manifest + events.ndjson + checksums. We include both line-delimited JSON (ndjson) and optional CSV exports.
- Delivery methods & SLA:
  * Presigned S3 bundle: standard 24 business hours from request acceptance; expedited 4 hours with signed expedited approval and PO.
  * Streaming to SIEM: available via our secure webhook / TLS stream endpoint; throughput subject to quota.
  * API bulk export: for programmatic pulls (pagination + range filters), with pagination windows of up to 30 days per job.
- Encryption & keys: Hosted: server-side AES-256; Dedicated: CMEK via AWS KMS (customer-managed); Private: HSM/KMS integration supported (documentation included).
- Legal hold: we can place a tenant-level preservation hold preventing deletion/export truncation; for Hosted customers this is time-boxed and requires agreement.

Validation steps (short):
1) Provide a bucket and role/STS details OR accept a presigned package.
2) We generate a sanitized sample presigned URL (see s3_presigned_sample.txt) for your infra team to verify object layout and ACLs.
3) Once validated, submit an export request via our portal or API (we'll include sample cURL in the playbook).

If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute walkthrough this week. Proposed times: Thu 3/25 10:00-10:30am ET or Fri 3/26 2:00-2:30pm ET. 

Attachments: redwood_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx, export_playbook_v1.pdf, s3_presigned_sample.txt
